**Resubmitted: T4C — deviation (high severity), preferred level, ok:true.**

Repairs made in response to the verifier:

1. **Party identification (the deterministic failure):** the inserted clause now expressly designates our party as the **"Customer"** — `Teleglobe USA Inc. (the "Customer")` — and the refund runs "to the Customer". The operative right is unchanged in substance (an unconditional unilateral Customer election, i.e. a convenience right) but is now stated in the checklist's own vocabulary, so "Customer convenience termination present" reads true on its face.

2. **Express numbering:** the clause now carries "18.1A" in its operative text as well as in the numbering field. This closes the tidiness gap the verifier identified: an unnumbered paragraph sitting inside the 18.1 block could have been argued to fall within the retained sentence "No credit for capital costs will be made to a Party that terminates its participation in accordance with Subparagraph 18.1." Our withdrawal is now unambiguously under 18.1A, so that forfeiture cannot attach to it.

Unchanged and deliberately so:

- **Level:** preferred, completed at one level (Customer right, 30 days' written notice, pro-rata refund of prepaid amounts). The 60–90 day fallback window is not pursued, as the verifier confirmed single-level completion suffices and preferred is more favourable to us.
- **Element 4 already_met** on the verbatim 18.1 quote — no reciprocal grant or restatement added for the counterparties.
- **Minimality:** one insertion, no deletions; the 25-year commitment, 18.2 unanimity/90% mechanic, paragraph 23 default remedies, and the capital-cost sentence (handled under LD) all left intact. No survival tail, expense, damages, or procedural add-ons.
- **Scope of the override:** "Notwithstanding Subparagraph 18.1" reaches only the timing bar, leaving the other Parties' one-year end-of-term exit and all commercial mechanics operative, with no dangling cross-reference.
